name: Boeing 717
summary: Final derivative of the DC-9 line, a 110-seat rear-engined twinjet flown in the US by Delta (now being retired) and Hawaiian.

wings: Low-mounted swept wing with plain tips — no winglets
Wing set relatively far back on the fuselage
engines: Two Rolls-Royce BR715 turbofans in pods on the rear fuselage sides
fuselage: 5-abreast fuselage — fatter than a regional jet, slimmer than a 737
Classic DC-9 nose with many small cockpit windows and a short, rounded profile
Short landing gear, sitting low to the ground
tail: T-tail with a pointed bullet fairing where the tailplane meets the top of the fin
Swept fin with a straight leading edge

tellTales: Engines on the rear fuselage and a T-tail on a mainline-size jet
Pointed bullet fairing at the top of the fin

confusedWith.howToTell: The 717 has a fatter 5-abreast body, plain wingtips and a bullet fairing on the T-tail; the CRJ700/900 is slimmer with winglets and a long pointed nose.
The 717 is much larger with a wider body and no winglets; the CRJ200 is a small, slender 4-abreast jet with winglets.
The 717 has a stubby, fat fuselage and plain wingtips; the ERJ145 is a very thin 3-abreast tube with a long pointed nose.

usCount.source: Delta (~74 after 2026 retirements) and Hawaiian (19) fleet data; InsideFlyer / Wikipedia Delta fleet
